shortlist.rationale: Four firm contracts awarded to the acquired subsidiary STEAG total Rs 5,112 cr over five years, which is 151% of FY26 revenue of Rs 3,382 cr (about 30% a year on the five-year term); the STEAG base sits outside the consolidated figures. The new awards of Rs 3,487 cr are about 7.6 times the company's own full-year FY26 new contract value and add power O&M as a new vertical, so they are not routine; the Rs 1,625 cr of renewals are continuity only. No disqualifier is shown: STEAG is described as net cash, and the company's TTM loss of Rs 23 cr is small with falling debt.

result.mechanism: Bluspring acquired 100% of STEAG Energy Services (India) on 21 May 2026 and its subsidiary won four long-term power-plant O&M contracts: BALCO Rs 2,050 cr (new, 1,740 MW, from 1 July 2026), VAML Rs 1,219 cr (renewal with increased scope), VPL Rs 406 cr (renewal) and VAML Rs 1,437 cr (new, 1,215 MW, from 1 August 2026). Total stated Rs 5,112 cr over five years, with STEAG's FY26 revenue of about Rs 700 cr sitting outside the consolidated base.
result.rationale: Four firm contracts awarded to the acquired subsidiary STEAG total Rs 5,112 cr over five years, which is 151% of FY26 revenue of Rs 3,382 cr (about 30% a year on the five-year term); the STEAG base sits outside the consolidated figures. The new awards of Rs 3,487 cr are about 7.6 times the company's own full-year FY26 new contract value and add power O&M as a new vertical, so they are not routine; the Rs 1,625 cr of renewals are continuity only. No disqualifier is shown: STEAG is described as net cash, and the company's TTM loss of Rs 23 cr is small with falling debt.
result.what_changed: The company adds power O&M as a new vertical with a multi-year annuity book, sharply raising its revenue base (company claims over 20% uplift to topline and 90-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion). The new awards of Rs 3,487 cr are about 7.6 times the company's full FY26 new contract value of Rs 459 cr, and the Rs 1,625 cr of renewals only continue existing business.
contradictions: The Rs 5,100 cr headline is cumulative five-year contract value for STEAG, not the company's order book; Rs 1,625 cr of it is renewals of existing contracts
Company-level TTM PAT is a loss of Rs 23 cr and TTM operating margin is 1.2%, so the uplift depends on STEAG's margin and the acquisition's cash effect
Consolidated FY26 base excludes STEAG (acquired 21 May 2026); the company's pro-forma uplift claim is not verifiable from the packet
result.next_milestone: Commencement of the BALCO O&M contract on 1 July 2026 and the VAML contract on 1 August 2026; first consolidated STEAG revenue in the Q2 FY27 results

result.mechanism: Contract wins from facility-management, food and industrial services clients; the trigger is the company's FY26 total annual contract value of Rs 459 crore across 164 contracts.
result.rationale: The 459 crore is a full-year FY26 total of 164 contracts (13.6% of FY26 revenue 3,382 crore), which is a period total and overlaps the 110 and 278 crore H1 and 9M disclosures, so it is noise rather than a new event (fatal flaw). Winning service contracts is the company's normal flow, so it is routine; the thin-margin (TTM OPM 1.2%) and cheap-valuation (market cap 0.3x revenue) exception applies, but the order would need TTM revenue growth above zero and revenue fell about 2.9% over FY26, so it is WATCH at most. No new operating event is shown beyond routine contract flow, so the outcome is a rejection, not a watch.
result.what_changed: The 459 crore figure is the full-year FY26 total of many contracts already reported as H1 (110 crore) and 9M (278 crore) figures, so it adds no new event; annual revenue fell 2.9% (3,483.6 to 3,382.0 crore) and margin recovery is from a low base.
contradictions: Trigger 459 crore is a cumulative FY26 period total, overlapping the 110 and 278 crore H1 and 9M disclosures
missing_information: TTM revenue growth not shown in packet; computed FY26 vs FY25 annual revenue change is -2.9%
Acquisitions of Nov 2025, Mar 2026 and Apr 2026 not assessed (text not extracted)
Product launch (brand identity refresh) is not an operating event

events.quote: The company is debt-free and has a free cash balance of INR 57 crores in addition to deposit given to BIAL.
In STEAG, we won four large contracts in India, which contribute to over INR5,200 crores to Bluspring’s top line over the next five years.

We foresee that it should be closed around 45 days and the water should settle down there, including the large contracts that we have won because some of the contracts that we have also won was to the customers that we had already worked towards and we know that what is the cycle there.
1. STEAG-BALCO contract worth Rs. 2,050 Crores June 5, 2026
2. STEAG-Vedanta Aluminium Metal Limited contract worth June 26, 2026 Rs. 1,219 Crores
3. STEAG-Vedanta Power Limited contract worth Rs. 406 June 26, 2026 Crores
4. STEAG-Vedanta Aluminium Metal Limited (VAML) July 3, 2026 contract worth Rs. 1,437 Crores The above information will also be available on the website of the Company at www.bluspring.com.
won 4 long-term deals adding to a cumulative contract value of over ₹5,100 Cr:
down subsidiary of the Company, has been awarded an order for Operations and Maintenance of
step-down subsidiary of the Company, has received an extension of contract for Operations and
step-down subsidiary of the Company, has received an extension of contract for Operations and
down subsidiary of the Company has been awarded an order from Bharat Aluminium Company Limited
In FY26, we have secured new 164 contracts with a total annual contract value of INR 459 crores.

These services contribute 90% of STEAG India's revenue base and are typically secured through long-term contracts ranging from three to five years, providing strong visibility into stable and recurring cash flows.
Our interest cost reduced sequentially by 41% to a steady state of around INR 5 to 6 crores per quarter.
We continued on our previously stated trajectory on reducing debt.
In nine months, we have secured new contracts worth ₹278 crore across Facility Maintenance, Food, and Industrial verticals.
• New sales continue to be strong in Q3, with business winning contracts worth ₹ 79 crore ACV.

• In the Industrials sub-segment, our focus on transitioning from a manpower provider to a strategic operations partner continues to yield results, as we won a ₹20 crore ACV contract for consolidated electrical and instrument maintenance for a large manufacturing client.
Excluding this, Industrial vertical has won ₹51crore ACV worth of contracts in 9 months FY26.
We continue on our previously stated trajectory of reducing DSOs and net debt levels.

Our debt has reduced by INR 29 crores quarter-on-quarter and as I mentioned earlier, that we believe that our cash generation is usually robust in Q4 and we have guided the markets that we will be a OCF to EBITDA ratio of around 50%.
We had done a fundraise for foundit back in 2022 and we had also taken borrowings at foundit level to the extent of close to around INR 50-odd crores.
So foundit has been funded basis the previous fundraise and the debt levels that have been raised at foundit level.

Kamal Pal Hoda: We would have invested close to around INR 250-odd crores, but that's not just our investment, this also includes the fundraise for which the money was also raised from the investors outside of Bluspring.
Bluspring Unveils Refreshed Brand Identity Post Demerger

• Introduces new brand identity symbolizing progress and forward momentum; brings together unified capabilities across infrastructure services under one integrated brand India, December 16, 2025: Bluspring Enterprises Limited (NSE: BLUSPRING, BSE: 544414), India’s leading integrated infrastructure management services company, today unveiled its refreshed brand identity, introducing a new logo and visual language.
In H1 FY '26, we have already secured 36 new contracts worth ₹110 crores across facilities, maintenance, food, and industrial verticals, setting us for growth in the coming quarters.
New sales have been strong in H1 with contracts worth ₹37 crores added only in Q2.
Then over the upcoming quarters, we look at reducing the debt obligation.
